DepositDef.label: fresh water
DepositDef.description: A river, a lake shore, or reliable rainfall close enough to draw on daily.

DepositDef.label: deep soil
DepositDef.description: Low, well-watered valley ground that breaks easily and holds a crop.

DepositDef.label: clay
DepositDef.description: Fine river-laid silt from a floodplain or a meander bend, good for pottery and daub.

DepositDef.label: flint
DepositDef.description: Nodules in dry lowland ground, knapped for blades and strike-a-lights.

DepositDef.label: stone
DepositDef.description: Rock close enough to the surface to quarry for walls and foundations.

DepositDef.label: ore
DepositDef.description: Metal-bearing rock in the hills and mountains, rarer the gentler the slope.

DepositDef.label: coal
DepositDef.description: Seams laid down in ancient swamp and floodplain ground, distinct from Ore's hills and mountains.

DepositDef.label: salt
DepositDef.description: Panned from a coastline, or rarely drawn from a mineral spring far inland.

DepositDef.label: timber
DepositDef.description: Standing wood, as thick as the local biome's own plant growth allows.

DepositDef.label: game
DepositDef.description: Huntable animal life, as plentiful as the local biome's own fauna allows.

DepositDef.label: ford
DepositDef.description: A shallow, low-lying river reach a band can cross on foot without a boat.

DepositDef.label: defensible ground
DepositDef.description: High ground over its surroundings, or a river bend that guards most sides at once.
